newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria adopts amendments to concession law.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria adopts amendments to concession law.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Wednesday passed on second and final reading amendments to a concession law in a bid to attract greater foreign investment.
Under the new law, concession rights will be granted on natural resources, enabling foreign firms which find oil or gas to redeem their investment if commercial use of the well proves worthwhile.

Concession rights were extended also to Black Sea beaches, radio frequencies, national posts and communications networks, water supply reserves, forests, nuclear equipment and public and state property.
Firms building new roads will be also granted concessions.
Concessions will be granted through tenders or competitions unless a state firm holds a 25 percent stake in a venture and its share is worth more than 300 million levs.
Deputies said the amendments to the initial Concession Law, which was adopted by parliament in October 1995, will help the cabinet speed up privatisation. -- Sofia newsroom +359-2 981 4145
